<section class="home-section">
  <h2>What I work on</h2>
  <ul class="work-list">
    <li>
      <div>
        <h3><a href="research.html#interdiction">Attacking congested networks where users route selfishly</a></h3>
        <p>An interdictor slows down roads on a budget; travelers settle into a new equilibrium. I compute the attack that hurts most, also when demand is uncertain, with two exact algorithms.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="status">Main PhD project, with Manish Bansal</div>
    </li>
    <li>
      <div>
        <h3><a href="research.html#microgrid">Risk-averse scheduling for a data-center microgrid</a></h3>
        <p>A two-stage stochastic MILP that limits energy shortfalls in the worst scenarios using CVaR, solved by Benders decomposition.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="status">With VT Electrical &amp; Computer Engineering</div>
    </li>
    <li>
      <div>
        <h3><a href="research.html#supply-chain">Pricing a product that is about to be withdrawn</a></h3>
        <p>A Stackelberg game between a manufacturer and two competing retailers when one of them may lose demand. Closed-form equilibria and when a retailer exits.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="status">Under review, Production Planning &amp; Control</div>
    </li>
    <li>
      <div>
        <h3><a href="research.html#tides">Making a tidal simulation actually run</a></h3>
        <p>Rebuilt my master's thesis solver for shallow-water equations, taking multi-cycle simulations from intractable to seconds.</p>
      </div>
      <div class="status">Manuscript in preparation</div>
    </li>
  </ul>
</section>

<section class="home-section">
  <h2>Background</h2>
  <div>
    <p>I'm a first-year PhD student in Industrial &amp; Systems Engineering at Virginia Tech, advised by Manish Bansal. I came to operations research from mathematics: an M.Sc. from NIT Calicut, where I graduated first in my class with the Institute Gold Medal, and a B.Sc. (Honours) from St. Stephen's College, Delhi.</p>
    <p>My tools are mixed-integer and bilevel programming, stochastic and distributionally robust optimization, and decomposition methods, implemented in Python and Gurobi and run at scale on a computing cluster.</p>
